meta.note: Archaeological / historical ages of the Indian subcontinent, used as the deep-time backdrop for the map. Boundaries are approximate and scholarly — regions transitioned at different times. Shown so you can see WHEN, in real deep time, each text-layer, event and proof sits.
meta.source: Standard South-Asian archaeology periodisation (e.g. Bronze Age = Indus/Harappan; Iron Age = Painted Grey Ware / Vedic; etc.).

ages.name: Bronze Age (Indus)
ages.note: Indus Valley / Harappan civilisation. Pre-dates the epics as texts.

ages.name: Iron Age (Vedic)
ages.note: Painted Grey Ware, later Vedic period — the milieu the epics look back to.

ages.name: 2nd Urbanisation
ages.note: Mahājanapadas, early historic cities, Buddhism — the epics begin to be compiled.

ages.name: Classical (Maurya→Gupta)
ages.note: Maurya, Kushan, Gupta. The epics reach their received textual form; the Gītā, Purāṇas.

ages.name: Early Medieval
ages.note: Regional kingdoms; the epics spread across Asia (Prambanan, Angkor); Kambaṉ.

ages.name: Modern
ages.note: Critical editions (BORI, Baroda); modern scholarship, translation, film.
